targets.authors: Conine, D. E., & Vollmer, T. R.
targets.title: Relative preferences for edible and leisure stimuli in children with autism.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of our study was to conduct a replication of Conine and Vollmer in Italy to evaluate cultural differences in food and leisure preferences.
targets.outcome_quote: Results of our study were similar: For 44% of participants, at least one leisure item ranked above all edible items and leisure items displaced all edible items for 28% of participants.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors report similar results on the central edible-versus-leisure displacement finding. Cultural differences concern which particular leisure items are preferred, an extension rather than a contradiction of that central finding.

reasoning: Title and five authors match publisher and PubMed. New Italian sample retests the immediately preceding Conine and Vollmer study; older food-displacement papers are background. Full text unavailable in indexed OA locations or Europe PMC; publisher HTML exposes abstract and references only. First online 2019, final volume 2020.
